newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: DuPont examines ICI Australia implications.
newsitem.headline: DuPont examines ICI Australia implications.

text.p: DuPont Australia chairman and chief executive John Foote said on Tuesday the U.S.-owned chemicals giant was on the lookout for acquisitions but had not formally expressed an interest in ICI Australia Ltd.

"I think any company would be looking today at what this decision might mean in terms of opportunities," Foote told Reuters in reference to the surprise decision last week by ICI Plc to sell its 62.4 percent stake in the Australian company.
"But we haven't made any expression of interest at this stage," Foote said.

ICI Plc said the controlling stake would be sold to institutional and retail investors, raising about A$2.2 billion to help fund the U.K. company's purchase of the specialty chemicals division of Unilver Plc/NV.
But the managing director of ICI Australia, Warren Haynes, said in a Sunday television interview that the company could, alternatively, be sold to a foreign bidder.

"They would have to make a bid for the whole company if they wished to do that, if that's what their strategy suggests and I suppose I shouldn't discount that as a possibility," Haynes said. He had been asked specifically if Dow Chemical Co or Hoescht Ag might be interested.
DuPont's Foote said he "absolutely totally surpised" that ICI Plc had chosen to offloat the Australian group rather than eventually launching a mop-up bid as most analysts and investors had expected.
He said the U.S. parent had a strategy to increase DuPont's Asia/Pacific sales to 20 percent of global revenue by the year 2000 from 10 percent, or about US$3 billion, at present.
This growth strategy, which included the US$500 million Australia and New Zealand market, would be achieved through organic expansion and acquisitions.
"I think any big company is always proactively looking at suitable acquisitions," Foote said.
"I mean we did acquire ICI's nylon business globally in 1993. We continue as always to look at value-adding acquisitions that are a fit with our core competences and skills."
ICI Australia shares were 20 cents higher at A$11.75 at 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT) on Monday, valuing the whole company at about A$3.5 billion.
